issues.failure_explanation: The even extension f̄^(l) satisfies f̄^(l)(0,z)=f^(l)(h,z) and f̄^(l)(±jh,z)=f^(l)(jh,z) for j≥1 (with ℏ=h). Hence the Poisson diagonal sum is h·Σ_{j=-∞}^∞ f̄^(l)(jh,z)=h f^(l)(h,z)+2r^(l)_{N_t}(z)+2hΣ_{j=N_t+1}^∞ f^(l)(jh,z), while ∫f̄ du=2I^(l)(z)+E_fd^(l)(z) with E_fd^(l)(z)=2hf^(l)(h,z)+2∫_h^0 f^(l)du+2∫_{N_t h}^∞ f^(l)du. Subtraction yields the correct identity ∫f̄ du−hΣf̄(jh)=2E_Q^(l)(z)+E_fd^(l)(z)−hf^(l)(h,z)−2hΣ_{j=N_t+1}^∞ f^(l)(jh,z). The displayed identity in the proof omits the −hf^(l)(h,z) term, making it algebraically incorrect.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the missing term −hf^(l)(h,z) to the displayed identity and absorb its bound |hf^(l)(h,z)| = O(T^l e^{−T}) into the existing error terms in the subsequent inequality, yielding the same lower bound on |E_Q^(l)(z)| and hence the same convergence rates.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed identity converting the Poisson summation formula to the quadrature error is incorrect. However, the missing term |hf^(l)(h,z)| is bounded by O(T^l e^{−T}), the same asymptotic order as the other remainder terms E_fd^(l) and the tail sum already accounted for in the proof. Consequently the claimed quadrature error rates in eq:errquad0 and the convergence rates in Theorems mainthm, mainthm2, mainthmG, Corollary mainthm3, and Theorem corner all remain valid once the missing term is absorbed into the existing bounds.
issues.title: Missing diagonal term in Poisson summation to quadrature error conversion
issues.why_classification: A short, local correction to the displayed identity plus a routine absorption of the additional O(T^l e^{−T}) term into the existing bound preserves every stated claim and guarantee. No new lemma, construction, or proof restructuring is needed.
